note.text: Capital structure describes the financing mix, especially equity and longer-term debt. Equity includes owners’ funds and retained earnings; debt requires repayment under agreed terms. In the stated school share-capital model, authorised capital is the permitted nominal ceiling, issued capital the nominal value allocated, called capital the amount requested on issued shares, and paid-up capital the amount actually received. These are distinct from a share’s market price. Legal terminology and permitted payment schedules vary; the model does not announce an OHADA filing rule or minimum capital.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to distinguish equity from debt and relate nominal issued, called and paid-up capital in a stated textbook model. Builds on: shares, shareholder returns and company financing needs. Leads to: the practical calculation of capital amounts.

sections.heading: Understand the economics
sections.text: Capital structure describes the financing mix, especially equity and longer-term debt. Equity includes owners’ funds and retained earnings; debt requires repayment under agreed terms. In the stated school share-capital model, authorised capital is the permitted nominal ceiling, issued capital the nominal value allocated, called capital the amount requested on issued shares, and paid-up capital the amount actually received. These are distinct from a share’s market price. Legal terminology and permitted payment schedules vary; the model does not announce an OHADA filing rule or minimum capital.

sections.heading: Follow the local case
sections.text: An invented company may issue nominal shares but request only a stated instalment. If some called funds are unpaid, paid-up capital is below called capital. It may also borrow or retain earnings; neither is another issue of shares. Ordinary shares carry a residual ownership claim; preference shares have stated preferential rights. A debenture is a debt instrument. Reserve capital in some textbook treatments is uncalled capital reserved for a specified event, not retained-profit reserves.

sections.heading: Reason and check
sections.text: Label the quantity, value per share and stage first. In a consistent instalment example, authorised ≥ issued ≥ called ≥ paid-up nominal amounts. Check unpaid calls separately. Debt interest, preferred distributions and ordinary dividends have different terms; no payment is risk-free merely because the example names it.

questions.prompt: In a textbook capital model, {issued} shares of nominal value {nominal} CFA francs have been issued. Only {called} CFA francs per issued share has been called. Calculate nominal issued capital, not called capital.

misconceptions.explain: That is called capital, not full nominal issued capital.
That is nominal value per share, not the whole issue.

solution: Issued capital uses nominal value, even if only part has been called.
